price_records.billing_note: Standard pricing for prompts with 272,000 or fewer total input tokens; cached prompt tokens are included and the selected tier applies to the full request.
Standard pricing for prompts with more than 272,000 total input tokens; cached prompt tokens are included and long-context rates apply to the full request.
Batch short-context pricing is the published 50% discounted rate and retains the whole-request 272,000-token boundary.
Batch long-context pricing is the published 50% discounted rate and applies to the full request above 272,000 total input tokens.
Flex short-context pricing uses the published Batch-equivalent rates and retains the whole-request 272,000-token boundary.
Flex long-context pricing uses the published Batch-equivalent rates and applies to the full request above 272,000 total input tokens.

notes: OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra on 2026-09-03. Public V1 fields intentionally project Standard short-context prices and Batch short-context input/output prices. Declarative price_records preserve Standard, Batch, Flex, and Fast short/long pricing, the whole-request 272K input-token threshold, cache-write charges, regional data-residency uplift, and the Fast EU data-residency exclusion. Priority is a routing alias for Fast and is not duplicated as a price record.

OpenAI lists promotional Standard pricing of $4 input, $0.40 cached input, $5 cache write, and $20 output per 1M tokens, available at least through 2026-11-21. Public V1 fields store Standard short-context prices and Batch short-context input/output prices. Prompts above 272K input tokens are billed at 2x input and 1.5x output for the full request; Pricing V2 also represents the published Batch, Flex, and Fast mode rates.

OpenAI official pricing and model documentation list Standard, Batch, Flex, and Fast rates per 1M tokens; Priority is an alias for Fast. Public V1 fields store Standard short-context prices and Batch short-context input/output prices. Prompts with 272K or fewer input tokens use short-context pricing; prompts with more than 272K input tokens use long-context pricing, with the selected tier applied to the full request. Pricing V2 represents the published short/long context prices for every processing mode.

OpenAI official pricing and model documentation list Standard, Batch, Flex, and Fast rates per 1M tokens; Priority is an alias for Fast. Public V1 fields store Standard short-context prices and Batch short-context input/output prices. Prompts with 272K or fewer input tokens use short-context pricing; prompts with more than 272K input tokens use long-context pricing, with the selected tier applied to the full request. Pricing V2 represents the published short/long context prices for every processing mode.

V1 stores Standard short-context input and output prices plus Batch short-context input and output prices. GPT-5.5 Pro does not offer a cached-input discount, so cached_input is null rather than zero. Long-context Standard pricing is $60 input and $270 output per 1M tokens; the current official pricing page does not list long-context Batch rates for GPT-5.5 Pro.
OpenAI official pricing page lists standard and batch rates per 1M tokens. Batch prices are 50% of the listed standard price where shown.

V1 stores Standard short-context input and output prices plus Batch short-context input and output prices. GPT-5.4 Pro does not offer a cached-input discount, so cached_input is null rather than zero. Above 272K input tokens, Standard pricing is $60 input and $270 output per 1M tokens; Batch pricing is $30 input and $135 output per 1M tokens.

V1 stores Standard short-context prices and Batch short-context input/output prices. Batch cached input is $0.125 per 1M tokens. Above 272K input tokens, Standard pricing is $5 input, $0.50 cached input, and $22.50 output per 1M tokens; Batch pricing is $2.50 input, $0.25 cached input, and $11.25 output per 1M tokens.
OpenAI official pricing page lists standard and batch rates per 1M tokens.
V1 stores Standard prices and Batch input/output prices. Batch cached input is $0.01 per 1M tokens. The official model page lists a 400K context window and no separate long-context pricing tier.

OpenAI lists the gpt-5 alias as Default and continues to publish Chat Completions, Responses, and Batch endpoints for it. Standard pricing is $1.25 input, $0.125 cached input, and $10 output per 1M tokens. The Batch guide states a 50% discount, represented in V1 as $0.625 input and $5 output. The dated snapshot gpt-5-2025-08-07 is deprecated and scheduled for API shutdown on 2026-12-11; OpenAI recommends gpt-5.6-sol as its replacement.

OpenAI lists gpt-4.1 with default snapshot gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 and continues to expose Chat Completions, Responses, and Batch endpoints. Standard pricing is $2 input, $0.50 cached input, and $8 output per 1M tokens. The Batch guide states a 50% discount, represented in V1 as $1 input and $4 output. No GPT-4.1 deprecation is listed in the current official deprecations documentation.

OpenAI lists the o3 alias as Default and continues to publish Chat Completions, Responses, and Batch endpoints for it. Standard pricing is $2 input, $0.50 cached input, and $8 output per 1M tokens; the model page also lists Batch pricing of $1 input, $0.25 cached input, and $4 output. The dated snapshot o3-2025-04-16 is deprecated and scheduled for API shutdown on 2026-12-11; OpenAI recommends gpt-5.6-sol as its replacement. V1 has no batch_cached_input field.

Anthropic lists base input, 5-minute cache write, 1-hour cache write, cache hit, and output rates. cache_write stores the 5-minute write rate; cache_write_1h stores the 1-hour write rate. Batch input and output are 50% of Standard; prompt-cache multipliers stack with the Batch discount.

Released 2026-09-01 and listed as Active (latest), with retirement not sooner than 2027-09-01. Standard pricing is $10 input, $0.25 cache read, $12.50 5-minute cache write, $20 1-hour cache write, and $50 output per 1M tokens. Batch input and output receive the published 50% discount.

Released 2026-09-01 and listed as Active (invite only) for approved Project Glasswing participants, with retirement not sooner than 2027-09-01. It shares Claude Fable 5.1 pricing: $10 input, $0.25 cache read, $12.50 5-minute cache write, $20 1-hour cache write, and $50 output per 1M tokens. Batch input and output receive the published 50% discount.
Anthropic table columns are input, 5-minute cache write, 1-hour cache write, cache read, and output. cache_write stores the 5-minute write rate.

Released 2026-07-24. Anthropic table columns are input, 5-minute cache write, 1-hour cache write, cache read, and output. cache_write stores the 5-minute write rate; cache_write_1h stores the 1-hour write rate. Batch pricing is 50% of standard input and output per Anthropic Batch Processing.

Standard pricing is $2 input, $0.20 cache hit, $2.50 5-minute cache write, $4 1-hour cache write, and $10 output per 1M tokens. Anthropic made the introductory rate permanent on 2026-08-10 and canceled the previously scheduled 2026-09-01 increase.
cache_write stores the 5-minute write rate.

Rates are for prompts up to 200k tokens. Google lists higher rates above 200k tokens in the official pricing table.
Rates are for text/image/video input; Google lists separate audio rates in the official pricing table.

Google applies Gemini 3.7 Flash introductory pricing to Gemini 3.6 Flash through 2026-12-31. V1 compatibility fields store the current Standard and Batch token rates. Structured pricing_periods preserves the 2027-01-01 Standard and Batch rates. Separate audio input and cache-storage charges are not represented in V1 scalars.

Generally available on 2026-08-13. V1 compatibility fields store introductory Standard and Batch token rates through 2026-12-31. Structured pricing_periods preserves the 2027-01-01 Standard and Batch rates. Separate audio input and cache-storage charges are not represented in V1 scalars.

Generally available and stable since 2026-09-02, with no shutdown date announced. V1 compatibility fields store the current Standard and Batch token rates through 2026-12-31. Structured pricing_periods preserves the 2027-01-01 Standard and Batch rates. The official cache-storage rates are not representable in the current canonical pricing-components schema.

V1 stores Standard input, context-cache, and output prices plus Batch input/output prices. Batch context caching is $0.075 per 1M tokens. Google also lists Flex and Priority tiers; those tiers are not represented in V1 pricing fields.

Generally available on 2026-08-26. Standard token pricing is audio input at $2 and text output at $12 per 1M tokens. Google estimates about $0.003/min for audio input, $0.002/min for text output, and about $0.005/min blended. Caching, Batch API, Flex inference, and Priority inference are not supported.

Generally available on 2026-08-26. Standard token pricing is audio input at $3.50 and text output at $21 per 1M tokens. Google estimates about $0.009/min blended. Caching, Batch API, Flex inference, and Priority inference are not supported.

Google released Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite generally available on 2026-07-21. V1 stores standard text/image/video rates and explicit Batch rates from the official pricing table. Separate audio rates are not represented. effective_from remains null because the official sources do not publish a distinct pricing effective date.

V1 stores Standard text/image/video input, context-cache, and output prices plus Batch input/output prices. Batch context caching is $0.0125 per 1M tokens. Separate audio rates are not represented: Standard audio input/cache are $0.50/$0.05 and Batch audio input/cache are $0.25/$0.025 per 1M tokens.

V1 pricing remains the short-context compatibility projection. Canonical Pricing V2 tiers model standard short-context prompt tokens < 200K and long-context prompt tokens >= 200K. Total prompt tokens include cached prompt tokens, and the selected tier applies to the whole request. Grok 4.3 Batch API pricing receives a 20% discount and is outside these standard tiers.

V1 stores short-context pricing. The long-context threshold is 200K tokens, where xAI lists $4 input, $0.60 cached input, and $12 output per 1M tokens. xAI Batch API documentation explicitly says Grok 4.5 is not supported, so Batch fields remain null. The 2026-07-16 announcement date is not used as effective_from because xAI does not publish a distinct pricing effective date.

Available on the xAI API since 2026-08-12. V1 stores short-context pricing. Canonical Pricing V2 tiers model standard prompt tokens < 200K and long-context prompt tokens >= 200K. Total prompt tokens include cached and non-cached prompt tokens, and the selected tier applies to the whole request. The xAI model page marks Batch API as not supported, so Batch fields remain null.

V1 compatibility pricing uses the conservative Peak rate. Actual pricing depends on UTC request time; Off-peak is 50% lower. Current official Peak hours are 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday; all other times, including weekends, are Off-peak. The price rates took effect at 2026-08-16T16:00:00Z. The official sources do not establish when the weekday-only schedule began, so schedule_effective_from is unknown.

V1 compatibility pricing uses the conservative Peak rate. Actual pricing depends on UTC request time; Off-peak is 50% lower. Current official Peak hours are 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday; all other times, including weekends, are Off-peak. The price rates took effect at 2026-08-16T16:00:00Z. The official sources do not establish when the weekday-only schedule began, so schedule_effective_from is unknown.

Mistral's current documentation maps mistral-large-latest to Mistral Large 3 (mistral-large-2512), which remains GA and available through Chat Completions and Batch. Standard pricing is $0.50 input, $0.05 cached input, and $1.50 output per 1M tokens. Cached prompt tokens are billed at 10% of standard input, and Batch processing receives a 50% discount, represented in V1 as $0.25 input and $0.75 output. The official docs do not separately specify whether cached-input and Batch discounts combine.

Cohere lists command-a-plus-05-2026 as Live and available through standard API endpoints, with no deprecation date. Its model page says both trial and production keys are free until rate limits are reached, while general pricing documentation says generative models including Command A+ are priced per token and the public pricing page says production keys are billed pay-as-you-go without publishing a Command A+ token rate. Standard Model Vault is a separate managed deployment option and lists Command A+ at $57.50 per XL instance-hour. V1 keeps Standard token, cached-input, and Batch prices null; null is not zero.
Cohere official pricing page lists Command R+ 08-2024 at $2.50/1M input tokens and $10.00/1M output tokens.
Cohere official pricing page states Aya Expanse 8B and 32B API pricing is $0.50/1M input and $1.50/1M output.

Cohere Parse v5 is generally available through the Cohere Parse API as parse-v5.0 at $1.50 per 1,000 pages. The public official sources do not publish a separate async or Batch API rate, page-count tier, or API free allowance. The free Cohere Space is a product demo, not a free API billing tier.

Current billing remains $0.01 per input image, $0.05 per 1K output image, and $0.07 per 2K output image. xAI began the retirement notice on 2026-09-02. Effective 2026-11-02, the old slug is scheduled to remain resolvable and redirect to grok-imagine-image-2.0 with quality=low; billing then follows the redirect target configuration. This scheduled transition does not change current prices.

Low quality billing is $0.01 per input image, $0.04 per 1K output image, and $0.06 per 2K output image. The quality selector is explicit because redirected requests from grok-imagine-image-quality are scheduled to use quality=low.
